proposal.body:
The current lockfile has 10 audited affected packages (one critical, eight high and one moderate). This updates Next/ESLint to 16.3.8, axios to 1.20.0, undici to 7.29.1, and compatible brace-expansion/ip-address resolutions. It also removes the unpatched braces/micromatch/fast-glob lint chain. Fresh production-only and development-inclusive audits at 59b65de81b52db2e29cde2d5848436661d04e631 both exit 0 with zero findings.

Next's pinned lint plugin is the only locked consumer of fast-glob and uses its directory-root globSync API. The private 0.0.0-flujo.1 adapter delegates to pinned tinyglobby 0.2.17 with literal-directory expansion disabled and absolute-root behavior preserved. It is explicitly a local adapter, not an upstream fast-glob release. Tests reject new consumers or unsupported caller APIs and exercise the actual Next root lookup and navigation lint rule, including dotted/space-containing Windows paths, root arrays, brace patterns and directory-only results. No lint rule or audit gate is disabled.

Validation on Windows/Node 22:
- Fresh locked npm ci, local dependency verification and npm ls passed.
- Five actual-caller/lint-rule assertions passed; seven focused model/request-boundary suites passed 159 assertions with no skips.
- Full lint:all and explicit adapter lint passed; git diff --check passed.
- The runtime-patch precursor 10d581ba74bcaa7d4d14469deddac51fe5af613a passed root typecheck and the default-heap production build. The build retained createRequire parsing warnings in codexRestrictedProfile; it is not an installed-worker/model qualification.
- Fresh CI must build/test the final exact revision on Windows/Linux before integration/release. Local audit receipts and raw test output are retained for #583's evidence ledger.

Upstream references: [Next advisory](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j), [braces advisory with no published fix](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm), [tinyglobby API](https://github.com/SuperchupuDev/tinyglobby). Earlier failed audits and incompatible-alias probes remain retained.

Refs #565 and #563. This removes a dependency gate blocker; it does not close the full scorecard or qualify a deployed release.
